newsitem.title: USA: Possible cold in Brazil coffee next week -- Cropcast.
newsitem.headline: Possible cold in Brazil coffee next week -- Cropcast.

text.p: Weather forecaster Cropcast said Wednesday long-range guidance models show Brazil's coffee belt could see colder temperatures late next week, with the probability of a freeze set at 15 percent.

"The potential for freezing temperatures late next week does exist," Cropcast said in its daily weather summery on Wednesday. "And this could result in damage to the coffee trees and next year's crop."

In its extended outlook, Cropcast said the latest long range model guidance suggested that an area of 1036 mb high pressure centered over Chubut, Argentina, on Aug 6 could track north-northeastward toward La Pampa, Argentina by the next day. By Aug 8, the system is expected to be over northern Santa Fe and southern El Chaco, Cropcast said.

"This track is suggesting that the Brazilian coffee regions could see temperatures at or slightly below 32 F (0 C) either on Saturday, Aug 9, or Sunday, the 10th," it said. "Given that this event is still a good way off, the probability of a freeze across the belt has been set at 15 percent."
Weather Services Corp meterologist Mike Palmerino warned, however, that long-range weather models can be "highly unreliable."

"I can't dispute what might be something of a change in pattern later next week, but it is so far out," said Palmerino. "The model goes out 10 days and it becomes unreliable when it goes out that far, but at least it is showing something different than no frost in sight."
He added, "It is still mid-winter. It is still a vunerable period for cold weather."

In its weather outlook this morning, Weather Services Corp said there is no damaging cold weather expected during the next seven days in Brazil's coffee belt, with low temperatures in the 50s to low 60s F (low to middle teens C).
